title: Annotatio I §.IV close IMPLICITE Pontificii: Double trope under the species — stop before Lutheran IMPLICITE
pass_a_gloss: But IMPLICITE whoever hitherto have interpreted that proposition otherwise than the Reformed make it tropical — both Pontificians and Lutherans — both sides nonetheless fighting explicitly for the propriety of the words as for hearths and altars. The PONTIFICIANS, having interpreted This is my body by this: That which is contained under the species of bread and wine is my body, expressly show a double trope in it — first Synecdoche, when this (which demonstrates substance with accidents) is determined to belong properly to the accidents; then Metonymy of Container for Contained. I pass over in silence one saying that the Proposition This is my body signifies as much as under these species or accidents is my body — in the very thing denying those words are to be taken properly and as they sound, and by his own ἔκθεσις overthrowing the hypothesis. The solid reason of the assertion is that in this way is perverted (1) the seat of Subject and Attribute: for my body becomes the Subject, and This the Attribute. Then the sense of the voice This is falsely and unlearnedly exchanged for those words under This, or under these species i.e. accidents, which differ by a whole category genus — Gomarus loc. cit. p. 142 nos. 63–64.
pass_b_english: IMPLICITE, whoever interprets the proposition otherwise than the Reformed also make it tropical — Pontificians and Lutherans alike — even while both fight explicitly for word-propriety as for hearth and altar.
The Pontificians’ That which is contained under the species of bread and wine is my body embeds a double trope: synecdoche (this → accidents) and metonymy of container for contained.

Swap This is my body for under these accidents is my body and you deny proper hearing in the act — subject and attribute seats flip, and This is falsely traded for under these species (Gomarus, p. 142).
Stop before Lutheran IMPLICITE readings (Luther’s in/cum/sub; Flacius’s duplex mass).
source_text: IMPLICITE vero tropicam efficiunt propositionem quicunque hactenus aliter quam Reformati, eam interpretati sunt, tam Pontificii, quàm Lutherani, utrique tamen explicitè pro proprietate verborum, tanquam pro aris & focis, dimicantes. PONTIFICII propositionem: Hoc est corpus meum, interpretati per hanc: Id quod continetur sub speciebus panis & vini, est corpus meum, duplicem tropum ei inesse disertè ostendunt, primò Synechdochen, quum hoc (quod demonstrat substantiam cum accidentibus) ad accidentia propriè pertinere statuitur; deinde Metonymiam Continentis pro Contento. Taceo, dicentem, Propositionem, Hoc est corpus meum, tantundem significare, quantum, sub hisce speciebus seu accidentibus est corpus meum, re ipsâ negare verba illa propriè & ut sonant, accipienda, suâque ἐκθέσει hypothesin subvertere. Assertionis ratio solida est, quia hoc modo pervertitur (1) Subjecti & Attributi sedes: nam corpus meum fit Subjectum, & Hoc, Attributum. Deinde, sensus vocis, Hoc, falso & indoctè permutatur verbis istis, sub Hoc, vel sub hisce speciebus i. e. accidentibus, quae toto categoriae genere differunt, Gomar. loc. cit. p. 142. num. 63. 64.
